T: Family dinner. Fake family. Real food.
D: Natasha reunites with the fake family she grew up with to bring down the Red Room.
P: Serve the mains when the whole fake family sits down to dinner at Melina's farm.
S: Fried puffed dough with garlic butter, sour cream and grated cheddar
Fried yeasted dough rounds brushed with garlic butter, spread with sour cream and topped with grated cheese.
almonds and cashews roasted glassy with sea salt, apricot and dark choc chunks, in paper bags

Almonds and cashews roasted in honey, chilli and sea salt until glassy, tossed with dried apricots and dark chocolate chunks, in little paper bags. Toss 200g almonds and 200g cashews with 3 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp melted butter, 1/2 tsp chilli flakes and 1 tsp sea salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 15 minutes, stirring halfway, until glossy and golden. Cool completely so they crisp up, then break apart. Mix with 100g chopped dried apricots and 100g dark chocolate chunks and portion into little paper bags.
Rye crispbreads with crème fraîche, smoked salmon, cucumber and dill
Rye crispbread spread with crème fraîche, topped with folds of smoked salmon, thin slices of cucumber, dill and a squeeze of lemon.
M: Seared pork chops roasted with apples and onions, mashed potatoes, braised cabbage

Pork chops seared and roasted with apples and onions, with mashed potato and braised cabbage. Sear 4 pork chops until golden, then add sliced apples and onions to the pan and roast at 200C for 15 minutes. Mash 1kg potatoes with butter. Braise shredded cabbage in a little butter and water until soft. Serve it all on big plates.
chuck, beetroot, cabbage, carrot and potato in a crimson broth with dill, sour cream, dark rye

Beef, beetroot, cabbage, carrot and potato simmered in a deep red broth with dill, finished with sour cream and dark rye bread. Brown 600g diced beef chuck in oil, cover with 2L water and simmer 1 hour. Add 3 grated beetroots, 2 grated carrots, 1 diced onion and 2 diced potatoes and cook 20 minutes. Add a quarter of a shredded cabbage, 2 tbsp tomato paste and 2 tbsp red wine vinegar and simmer 15 minutes more. Season well, stir through chopped dill and serve with sour cream and rye bread.
W: Vanilla cupcakes piped with pastel buttercream and sprinkles
Vanilla butter cake batter spooned into patty pans, baked at 175C for 18 minutes, cooled and piped with pastel buttercream and sprinkles.
K: Red Guardian's black tea with cherry jam
Strong black tea stirred with strawberry jam, served hot in glasses with lemon

Strong black tea brewed with lemon and a spoon of jam stirred in, served in glasses. Brew a strong pot of black tea with 4 tea bags and a litre of boiling water for 5 minutes. Pour into heatproof glasses and stir a spoon of strawberry jam into each. Add a slice of lemon and serve hot, family style.

s.note: Fried puffed dough with garlic butter, sour cream and grated cheddar
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast and 300ml warm water to a soft dough and prove an hour. Stretch into rounds and fry in hot oil until puffed and golden. Brush with butter mixed with crushed garlic, then spread with sour cream and top with grated cheddar.

s.note: Rye crispbreads with crème fraîche, smoked salmon, cucumber and dill
s.how: Spread rye crispbreads with crème fraîche. Top each with folds of smoked salmon, thin cucumber slices and a sprig of dill. Squeeze over a little lemon just before serving, the kind of snack you eat at a safe house in the north.

m.note: Seared pork chops roasted with apples and onions, mashed potatoes, braised cabbage

w.note: Vanilla cupcakes piped with pastel buttercream and sprinkles
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Spoon into patty pans and bake at 175C for 18 minutes. Cool and pipe with pastel buttercream made with icing sugar, then cover with sprinkles.
